model: Daintree DCS WAC root device (BACnet IP)
applies_to: The root BACnet device of each Daintree Wireless Area Controller (WAC) managed by Daintree Controls Software.
summary: Each Daintree WAC runs its own BACnet IP server. The root device is a router that represents the WAC itself; lighting and sensor zones appear as separate virtual devices behind it. The root device only carries two health points: the WAC's link to the configuration server and the state of its ZigBee network.
default_device_instance: Set in DCS (BACnet Router Device ID)
notes: Device name is the WAC name from DCS, or its MAC address if none is set.
Lighting zones and sensor zones are separate virtual devices; see the Daintree DCS lighting zone and sensor zone lists.

source.title: Daintree Controls Software (DCS) BACnet integration guide

integration.summary: Enable BACnet on the gateway in DCS and set the router device ID and virtual network numbers. Monitor the two status MVs on the root device to know whether the WAC and its wireless network are healthy; control happens on the zone devices.
setup: Set in DCS (Configure > Gateway > BACnet settings): router device ID, network number, virtual network number, start/end virtual zone device IDs, NIC (wan or building), port (normally 47808).
Foreign device registration to a BBMD is available when the WAC is not on the BMS LAN.
The WAC routes BACnet IP to a virtual network; each zone is its own virtual device (B-ASC profile).
gotchas: The two WAC ports (wan RJ45 and USB-Ethernet building) must not be on the same subnet.

points.name: Server Connection Status
points.description: Link between WAC and the configuration server

points.name: ZigBee Network Status
points.description: Whether the WAC's ZigBee network is running
